Let's look at the possible diagnoses:
drug reaction, allergy, chicken pox, diabetes, psoriasis, hypertension, cervical spondylosis, bronchial asthma, varicose veins, malaria, dengue, arthritis, impetigo, fungal infection, common cold, gastroesophageal reflux disease, urinary tract infection, typhoid, pneumonia, peptic ulcer disease, jaundice, migraine.

Symptoms analysis:
- Burning pain in stomach (epigastric pain)
- Gas and bloating
- Weight loss, loss of appetite
- Dark and tarry stools (melena)
- Blood in vomit (hematemesis)

These are classic signs of Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD). Melena and hematemesis indicate upper GI bleeding, which is a complication of peptic ulcers. Burning epigastric pain is also typical.

Let's check the reference examples:
[1] Q: I have a burning feeling in my stomach... A: peptic ulcer disease
[18] Q: I have a stomach pain that keeps me up at night. I get tired after using the bathroom and I don't want to eat. I worry all the time. A: peptic ulcer disease
[20] Q: I have been having frequent headaches, stomach acid, indigestion, hazy and distorted vision, increased appetite, stiff neck, depression, irritation, and visual distortion. A: peptic ulcer disease

Wait, [20] says "peptic ulcer disease" but lists weird symptoms? Maybe it's just a noisy reference. But [1], [18], [20] all point to peptic ulcer disease for stomach pain/burning/acid.
Also, melena and hematemesis strongly point to peptic ulcer disease.

Let's verify against other options:
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD): heartburn, acid reflux, sore throat, bad breath, vomiting. Doesn't typically cause melena or hematemesis (though severe esophagitis can bleed, PUD is more classic for these).
- Typhoid: diarrhea, stomach ache, vomiting, fever, weakness.
- Jaundice: yellow skin, dark urine, abdominal pain, weight loss, itching.
- Malaria/Dengue: fever, rash, headache, body pain.

So "peptic ulcer disease" is the best match.
